themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions in Flushing have deteriorated sharply THIS WEEK, with 243 complaints filed compared to a 53.6-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 353% spike (z-score: 9.29)—suggesting infrastructure failure or weather damage requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 243 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 53.6 weekly average (353% spike, z-score 9.29)
Street Sweeping Complaint spike: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.2 average (1900% increase, z-score 10.97)
Community Board has standing request for street infrastructure investment from Economic Development Corporation
reporting_angles: On-the-ground assessment: map complaint hotspots and photograph conditions in high-complaint areas
Interview DOT about maintenance backlog and whether budget constraints are delaying repairs

themes_detail.label: Noise Surge in Public Spaces
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints in Flushing spiked 497% THIS WEEK to 97 complaints versus a 16.2-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 8.96), indicating either new construction, street activity, or enforcement failure.
evidence: 97 Street/Sidewalk Noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 16.2 weekly average (497% spike, z-score 8.96)
993 building permits filed in last 90 days (605 alterations alone), suggesting construction activity
Residential noise also remains chronically high: 1,649 complaints over 90 days
reporting_angles: Identify which construction or street activity is triggering this week's spike via permit records and NYPD noise enforcement logs
Interview residents in high-complaint neighborhoods about quality-of-life impact

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints in Flushing surged 600% THIS WEEK to 7 complaints versus a 1.0-complaint weekly average (z-score: 8.49), a potential signal of aging grid infrastructure, storm damage, or concentrated outages affecting multiple buildings.
evidence: 7 electrical complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (600% spike, z-score 8.49)
Related: Elevator complaints spiked 1500% two weeks ago (6 vs. 0.4 average), which may depend on electrical systems
Community Board has standing request for building inspector expansion from DOB
reporting_angles: Contact Con Edison to determine if localized outages, grid issues, or infrastructure work triggered complaints
Document whether building code violations or deferred maintenance in older Flushing buildings are a factor

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints in Flushing jumped 344% THIS WEEK to 10 complaints versus a 2.2-complaint weekly average (z-score: 6.46), suggesting new pest pressure coinciding with street condition deterioration and illegal posting activity.
evidence: 10 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average (344% spike, z-score 6.46)
Coincides with street condition spike (243 complaints) and illegal posting surge (45 complaints), both indicating neighborhood deterioration
Dirty Condition complaints: 477 over 90 days, baseline for pest-attractive conditions
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene on whether they've detected a neighborhood-level infestation and any response plan
Connect with residents and local businesses to understand whether new construction, street debris, or waste management failure is attracting rodents

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting & Visual Disorder
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints in Flushing spiked 368% THIS WEEK to 45 complaints versus a 9.6-complaint weekly average (z-score: 5.19), reflecting either reduced enforcement or a coordinated campaign affecting public space perception.
evidence: 45 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.6 weekly average (368% spike, z-score 5.19)
Overlaps with street condition and noise spikes, suggesting broader neighborhood disorder
Part of larger sanitation picture: 477 dirty condition complaints over 90 days
reporting_angles: Photo essay documenting posted surfaces across Flushing to show scope and nature of violations
Interview DSNY enforcement on staffing and response times for posting removal
